pages.title: Before interview day
pages.note: Formats differ by school: traditional one-on-one, panel, MMI or a mix, in person or virtual. Your invite email is the final word, and the AAMC's MSAR interview policies report is a good place to compare schools. You've got this!

items: Format from the invite: traditional, panel, MMI or a mix
In person or virtual (note the time zone!)
Length of the day and the full schedule
Anything due before the day (forms, a survey)
Is the interview open or closed file?
Mission, in your own words
The community it serves and its health needs
2-3 things only this school offers (MSAR + its site)
Why this school, beyond the website copy
Re-read your personal statement
Re-read your Work and Activities
Re-read this school's secondary essays
A plain, honest answer for any gap or weak spot
Tell me about yourself (about 2 minutes)
Why medicine: the spark, what grew it, the doctor you want to be
A time you worked on a team
A challenge or mistake and what you learned
One full mock interview with a real person
MMI drills on a timer: short read, then talk
Ethics prompts: talk through both sides first

pages.title: Interview day log
pages.note: Fill in the log the same day, while it's fresh. Future you (and your thank-you notes) will be so grateful!

items: Test camera, mic and internet the day before
Quiet room, plain background, light in front of you
Link, login and a backup phone number saved
Notifications off, phone on silent
Route, parking and arrival time planned
Outfit tried on the night before
Water, a snack and your questions to ask
Be kind to everyone you meet that day
Names of everyone who interviewed me
One thing we talked about with each
Thank-you notes, if the school's policy allows them
My gut feeling about fit, written down today

pins.headline: Med school interview prep checklist
items: Know the format: traditional or MMI
Re-read your whole application
Practice "tell me about yourself"
Do one real mock interview
Log every question you're asked
